subtitulo: The no that never says no
introPt: A traveller reads a refusal correctly and saves three days.

dialogo.es: Eh, vediamo... magari più avanti, dai.
dialogo.pt: Well, we'll see... maybe further along, come on.
dialogo.tts: Eh, vediamo... magari più avanti, dai.

dialogo.es: Sì sì, certo, alle otto, ci sono. Tranquillo.
dialogo.pt: Yes yes, of course, at eight, I'll be there. Don't worry.
dialogo.tts: Sì sì, certo, alle otto, ci sono. Tranquillo.

dialogo.es: Guardi, signore, le ho già detto di no.
dialogo.pt: Look, sir, I've already told you no.
dialogo.tts: Guardi, signore, le ho già detto di no.

dialogo.es: Ma dammi del tu, per favore! Come ti chiami?
dialogo.pt: Oh, use tu with me, please! What's your name?
dialogo.tts: Ma dammi del tu, per favore! Come ti chiami?

perguntas.pergunta: What tells you it is a real yes?
opcoes: Speed, repetition and a concrete detail
perguntas.explica: A refusal arrives slowly, hedged, without specifics.

perguntas.pergunta: Guardi plus a switch to signore means:
Someone asks you to use tu. You should:
opcoes: Stay on lei to be safe
perguntas.explica: Refusing it reads as keeping distance.

perguntas.pergunta: Mi dica pure di no is:
opcoes: A normal, well-received sentence that gets you a real answer
perguntas.explica: Nobody is offended by an easy way out.

perguntas.pergunta: In a home, the signal that it is time to go is:
opcoes: Coffee having been served and drunk
perguntas.explica: Leaving before it reads as the evening having failed.
